questions.q: What does the summary say about trying hard to feel happy?
a: It can backfire and enlarge the negative thoughts
It reliably raises happiness over time
It works only for naturally optimistic people
It requires daily positive affirmations
questions.why: Lesson 1 says scanning for bad thoughts tends to strengthen them.

questions.q: What does the pink elephant effect demonstrate?
a: Trying to suppress a thought makes it more present
Positive images can replace sad memories
Distraction is the best cure for grief
People forget instructions quickly
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses it to explain why avoiding sadness often prolongs it.

questions.q: Why does positive visualization often fail?
a: It satisfies you early and drains your effort
It makes your goals seem unrealistic
It creates anxiety about the future
It only works for athletes
questions.why: Lesson 2 says imagining success makes people relax before doing the work.

questions.q: What is the benefit of imagining the worst case?
a: It builds resilience and curbs hedonic adaptation
It prepares you to give up early
It lowers your expectations permanently
It replaces the need for planning
questions.why: Lesson 2 says it keeps us from growing greedy and complacent.

questions.q: What does Burkeman recommend instead of desperate goal-chasing?
a: Approach goals with improvisational flexibility
Abandon all goals and drift
Commit harder to one identity-defining goal
Set goals only for your career
questions.why: Lesson 3 says determination can make us more stupid, not more successful.
